heading: INT. GENERATION SHIP "TERNARY LANTERN" - HYDROPONIC SPINE - SHIP NIGHT

units.text: INT. GENERATION SHIP "TERNARY LANTERN" - HYDROPONIC SPINE - SHIP NIGHT
A cylindrical corridor lined with trays of silver-leafed lettuce, each rotating slowly toward an artificial sun that is, tonight, a pale and dying amber.
JUNO ABARA-WESTLUND (30s, botanist, gloves stained green) kneels at a leaking pipe.
Beside her, an old gardener's robot of brass and canvas has stopped mid-sentence.
A second woman steps from the airlock: COMMANDER ISADORA FENN-KATSURAGI (50s, uniform pressed, hair cropped).
She looks at the pipe.
Looks at the amber light.
How long has the sun been failing?
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Eleven hours. I filed it.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: I read the file. She did not say eleven.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: She said eight. She was wrong. I corrected her.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: She holds up a wrench.
Her hand shakes, and it is not fear.
It is the long fury of a woman who has been right in a ship that does not want her to be.
Isadora's eyes narrow.
She takes a step closer, and the lettuce trays lean toward her like a congregation.
You rewrote the commander's log.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: I corrected it.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: Without permission.
units.name: ISADORA

units.text: Without waiting for her to die first.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: The amber light stutters.
The pipe hisses.
Neither woman looks at it.
